tb-E402-1.question:
Which of the following is/are reason(s) why the pressure applied on the oval window is larger than the pressure applied on the eardrum?

(1) Lever action occurs at the middle ear.

(2) The oval window has a smaller area than the eardrum.

(3) The acoustic impedance in the inner ear is much higher than that in the outer ear.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E402-1.reasoning:
The ossicles' lever action increases the force delivered to the oval window, whose area is smaller than the eardrum's. From p=F/A, both greater force and smaller area increase pressure.

The impedance difference explains why matching is needed, but is not itself the mechanical mechanism that amplifies pressure. Statements (1) and (2) are correct: A.

source.name: E402 Revision 2 Human Hearing and Ultrasound Scanning.docx

tb-E402-2.question:
Darwin is operating a machine which produces sound. The intensity of the sound is 3 × 10−3 W m−2 when reaching his ears. By wearing ear protectors, the sound intensity received by Darwin drops to 1 × 10−6 W m−2. Find the reduction in the sound intensity level.

A 4.8 dB

B 34.8 dB

C 60 dB

D 94.7 dB
tb-E402-2.reasoning:
L1 = 10 log (I1I0) ……(1)

L2 = 10 log (I2I0) ……(2)

Subtract (1) from (2):

L2 − L1 = 10[log(I2I0)-log(I1I0)]

= 10 log(I2I0÷I1I0)

= 10 log(I2I1)

= 10 log(1×10-63×10-3)

= −34.8 dB

The sound intensity level decreases by 34.8 dB.

tb-E402-5.question:
Figure b shows several curves of equal loudness of a person.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The lowest curve indicates the threshold of hearing of the person.

(2) Note P is louder to the person than note Q.

(3) The intensity of note P is about 100 times higher than that of Q.

A (1) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E402-5.reasoning:
The lowest curve is the equal loudness curve at 0 phon and therefore is the threshold of hearing of the person.

∴ (1) is correct.

Notes P and Q lie on the same equal loudness curve and therefore are perceived to have the same loudness.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

LP − LQ = 10 log(IPIQ)

20 = 10 log(IPIQ)

2 = log(IPIQ)

102 = IPIQ

IPIQ = 100

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-E402-14.question:
Figure f shows an ultrasound image of an internal organ. The ultrasound pulse enters the body through the skin. It then travels from medium X to medium Y, and finally to medium Z. Assume the acoustic impedances of media X and Z are the same.

(a) Johnson thinks that region Y appears dark because the attenuation of ultrasound in it is small. Comment on this statement. (2 marks)

(b) Suppose an ultrasound pulse of intensity 0.01 W m−2 is incident on the X−Y interface and the intensity reflected is 0.001 W m−2. Find the intensity reflected at the Y−Z interface, assuming that the attenuation in region Y is negligible. (3 marks)
tb-E402-14.answer:
(a) This statement is incorrect. 1A

Region Y appears dark because almost no reflection of ultrasound occurs in it. 1A

(b) Intensity reflection coefficient on the X−Y interface

= 0.0010.01 = 0.1 1M

Intensity reflection coefficient on the Y−Z interface

= intensity reflection coefficient on the X−Y interface

= 0.1

Intensity transmitted at the X−Y interface

= 0.01 − 0.001 = 0.009 W m−2

Intensity reflected at the Y−Z interface

= 0.009 × 0.1 1M

= 0.0009 W m−2 1A
